title: Saints C Erik McCoy on playing in primetime & representing New Orleans on Domecoming anniversary
text: Um, in a game like Monday, um, 2010, back in the Dome, so I guess there's just no bigger rivalry than that .    In your time here— you mentioned the Dome—what understanding have you gained of what the city went through with Katrina and what this team means to the community? Yes.  I mean, with all the adversity that the city has been through, I think when you're on a team, you see how connected the city and the team are: like when we're doing well, the city is upbeat, and if we're not playing well, the city is sad.  So I think we can be a ray of hope, a light for this city, and… We know that Coach showed the team old videos to give them an understanding of Katrina and Dome, but you were also on the team that had to evacuate because of another hurricane. How much did this experience help you better understand what was happening on Monday?    It helped a lot.  Well, of course, our displacement is nothing compared to what happened in 2005-2006, but it was still an unpleasant experience. You know, being far from home, from your city, training in another place, constantly traveling, every game as an away game—it's not very pleasant.  So I also give credit to the 2006 team for their resilience. They had 13 wins and 3 losses that year.  Yeah, 13-3 and a championship, that's...This is serious, it wasn't easy.  So respect to them. Does it add to the drive, especially to show everyone what has been built here all this time? Excellent question.  I cannot answer for others.  I think the importance of coming home is more significant to me than the fact that it's a prime-time game.  Ultimately, we just have to go out and play our football.  This is what we do every Sunday.  So we need to go out, execute our plan and play at the highest level.

They almost lost because of Jameis Winston.  They won despite him.  JJ McCarthy could give them a chance to not win despite their quarterback.  He can really control the game enough that they win and feel like the quarterback contributed.  If that's the case, they could win significantly more games because the schedule for the next few weeks indirectly becomes easier.  The next four opponents have a combined record of three wins and nine losses.  This is a time when the Giants should focus on winning games, and if they are consistently winning despite James, they should make a trade for a quarterback who is better suited to the offense, and that could be J.J. McCarthy.

title: Nick Sirianni on Facing the Los Angeles Rams
text: Nick, when you're coming when you're coming off tough losses like you guys are and you have some key guys who are injured and may or may not play, how does that challenge you as a coach? What what do you have to do to to make sure this stays where you guys need to be? >> You go regardless of whether you win or whether you lose, you go through the same process. I think I read something that Kobe said that is like you win, great, you got to get up and do the same thing. You lose, it sucks, but you got to get up and do the same thing. And yeah, I mean this is this you know, there's ups and downs in every season. There's there's high points, there's low points, there's wins, there's losses. And our you know, there's there's guys at times that are going to be in, there's guys at times that are going to be out. And our job is to, you know, go through the same process each each and every week. Um and be able to do our our jobs as as coaches to to account for the guys that that may not may or not be may or may not be playing. And for the guys that are stepping in for them to be ready to go. Um and that's why, you know, we do the things that we do at practice and and have the developmental periods where where guys get that extra work where they're getting, you know, the work on our plays. And so, um yeah, you just go you you I know it's boring and you probably could say, "Hey, that's just coach talk." But it really is you got to just you got to have faith in the process until the process produces results in every everything that you do. And so, you know, um business as usual was this week. And um I got a lot of faith with with all the guys in this building. That's why they're in this building. That's why they have a uh that's why they're on the team of of the Eagles is because we have faith in them and we know that each and every guy in our locker room can help us. >> Nick, with how big of a part of the offense DeVonta has been, how do you go about game planning for a game where he might not be able to play? >> Yeah, um you know, obviously he's a he's a great player. We'll see where we are at the end of the day um, and and by Sunday. Um, but, you know, you go you go through it the same way. You go through it and you think about the things that you do well and that your guys do well. Um, you think about the defense that you're playing and the things that you have to do there. Um, and you put guys in positions, you know, you you it's okay, we're running a a play that Smitty might be good at and he's the first reader, whatever it is. And then you say, "Hey, is this play still good?" And who who's the guy that should go in for that that situation? So, that's kind of how it goes. Um, you know, if of when you're getting ready for for anything like that and you have to do that you do that a lot. There's there's guys that are questionable all week that you do that with. Um, and you have backup and contingency plans and all those different things. So, um, it just it's again, it's just part of our process of of what we do on a on a weekly basis. >> I think you neck trusting everybody, specifically a wide receiver. What do you what do you trust about Darius Cooper and Elijah Moore specifically if they have to really step up and >> Yeah, I think that you've seen Coop with the things that since he's gotten here, I think you've seen him take all his responsibilities and really star in his role. Um, and so when that happens, you obviously have trust in him as Moore is called upon in his role. Um, you know, with with Elijah, I mean, the talent is is there. He he is a very talented football player. And you watch him run routes, it's pretty watching him run routes the way he gets in and out of breaks. And he's done and he's had a a lot of success in this league and I'm sure glad we have him on this football team cuz I know he can help us win football games. Um, you know, it's just like I said, he's got this great ability to get in and out of breaks to threaten vertical with speed and to finish with a catch and which is why he's been in the league and had the success that he's had. And so just really pumped that that you know, we have those guys and we have the depth that we have and that we've you know, worked hard to help develop that depth and those guys work hard to continue to develop themselves. >> Why do you think you've had success against Sean McVay? >> Um, you know, the good good teams, you know, good teams that against good teams, you know, I I think I have a ton of respect for uh coach McVay and all the coaches that are on that staff have been coached with a lot of those guys that are on the staff. I think three of them particularly on the defensive staff. I think they're phenomenal coaches. I think they got great players. I think we got great coaches. I think we got great players and as we know every one of those games could have went either way, right? How many of those games that we've played against the Rams that could go either way? I mean, particularly last year. You know, particularly the NFC divisional game. I know that I can't think back too much further than that, but the you know, just again so much respect there. You know, we've we've played good games. We've played good halves. You know, in those situations and you know, again all those games can go either way and I can't tell you how much respect I have for those guys over there, the players and and their coaches. Obviously Stafford's a heck of a quarterback. They got really good playmakers all over the place and and I think the world of Shawn and all and all his coaches. >> If Jeremiah Trotter Jr. has to go for a Zach Born, what makes you confident in him and just how much have you seen him grow from you know, the first two years to this year for a role like this if you >> Yeah. Yeah, he uh every every opportunity he's got and a chance to play, whether it's in preseason or in games, he's he's done a really nice job. Um now, that's not the only thing we're evaluating, right? We have to get to evaluate practice on a daily basis. He gets to go against, you know, our offense at times. Um and then, you know, also get reps in there with with the defense. He's been getting reps with the defense the entire year. And then, like I said, we have our developmental periods that he gets to get reps of our defense in as well. I think that's why it's so important that you mix those things in. Um so a guy's not strictly doing scout team and that and now in a situation like this, if he if he is called upon, that he's he's got to play without getting meaningful work on our on our defense. Um but I have faith in him because I think a lot of times you look at you look at linebackers and you're like, I mean, how are they going to do in a game um if they have to go in and and play play a lot? And I think that special teams is a great indicator of that, you know, the tackles that they have to make in space, the block destruction that they have to do, the physicality that they have to play with. Um you know, are a lot of signs of what lead to good linebacker play. Now, there's other stuff, obviously, as well, but that there's a lot of signs that point there and he's been one of our top special teams players the past 2 years that he's been here and then going on his third year uh being here. So, like I said, you know, like I said with the wide receivers, I love our depth. I love our depth there as well. You know, Smiles giving us really good uh really good things on special teams. Um and so, just another credit to Howie and his staff of the guys that they've brought in. A credit to Bobby King and Vic for the development of the guys. And and most importantly, a shout-out to the guys that are doing it because they are, you know, they're the ones that are the ta have the talent and are working hard to get better on on a daily basis. >> Couple more? >> Coaches offer different theories on halftime adjustments. How much time do you have to actually make adjustments at halftime and what's your halftime routine? >> Yeah, I mean obviously your I'm not going to get too much into our routine Zach, but you know, um the things that you have to it is a very short halftime and then you know, and then obviously we've had two games since I've been here that are a very long halftime. but it is a very short uh short process and that's why it's got to be that you're making adjustments as you go. Um and that's what's being talked about every every time. Hey, are they Hey, we're in this set. Are they playing what we thought? Cool. Okay, is this play that I mean that these are the conversations that are happening on the headset you know, in between series. When the defense is up, you know, it's the offense doing it. When the offense is up, it's the defense of that it's doing it. Um and that's so important that they're they're going through that process at the at that time because halftime, there may be a certain things that you say, okay, we can't get that drawn up right that Hey, we want to put this in here. Hey, we can't get that drawn up. Draw it up for halftime, we'll put it in there. So there there are some things that are are saved for halftime, but so much of the majority of it is happening within game because you got you got to think you have your TV timeouts, you got this long long break with the defense or the offense being on the field or in the special teams. And so that's where you're planning your next drive and you're planning your next drive based off of what you're thinking's happening and adjustments that you're making there. Now, you don't get into that real early. It's not like you've been there too is like it the first play is like, oh my gosh, they're running this versus that. Like what that's too early, right? Because you don't know exactly what the other team's game plan is saying quite at that time. So, it takes a little bit of time to get into the game to do it and then then you're doing that on a on a drive-to-drive basis. >> What have you seen from Zach Ertz and and Kenny Moore as far as picking up the playbook and obviously Zach played last week against >> Mhm. >> as far as being ready to play >> Yeah, those guys are are man, I've been able to coach been on the staffs that have coached they've been players on in the past. Um so I you know, I know that the guys are top-notch guys and are highly talented guys. and you know, they work their butts off and they've worked their not only on the field but off the field as well and and they're doing a good job of really picking it up and you know, and so because they work hard and they're and of who they are. So, I feel good about those guys and where they're >> All right.

title: Sean Mannion on Preparing For Los Angeles Rams
text: Sean, uh, what could you pinpoint to some of the second half struggles this year, including the Chicago game, and kind of what's your thoughts on those going forward? >> Yeah, certainly as a staff and as a team, we're working through getting better there. Um, you know, you hate to do a lot of nice things in the first half of some of these games and then and kind of fall into a rut in the second half. So, it's something uh, you know, we we've been we've been discussing, you know, each week looking to get sharper and sharper as a unit and as a staff. And, um, I think we got some good things to work on there. um some good um good thoughts moving into this week of how to how to improve on that because um you know you hate to have you know in the Tennessee game you have some good long drives and then and then you kind of stub your toe out of the gate in the second half and certainly that was you know that was the case in the Chicago game as well. So we're working at that. Um we're we're attacking it each day to be better there uh coming out of halftime stay ahead of schedule in the first half. Yeah. >> Um and yet the play action under center stuff >> wasn't there. You weren't didn't run much of it. what what were the some of the issues for not marrying as much of the pass off the run success there? >> Yeah, you know, I think some of it is, you know, varies based on the opponent, based on the defensive front you might be getting in terms of your protection plan and what things you can have up in the plan and not um like you said, you know, was really encouraged with the run game. You know, we we tried to build off of it and um you know, early in the game, you know, we had a we had a keeper, we know a tough look um early in the game there. We had a couple you know, things we just need to clean up in terms of the execution of our play pass protection. And ultimately I I I need to build the best plan possible to find that marriage. So um you know that's on me to to put us in the best position possible to build um our marriage of the running past the way we want it to look. Um you know cuz I think with the way we got the run game going there's more to maximize off of that. So like I said it starts with me and uh and I got to make sure I'm putting all of our guys in the best position to succeed. And uh and I think, you know, if we get the run game going the way it looked um last Monday, um I think there's there's a lot of big plays to be had in the play pass game. If we're just a little bit sharper um collectively and and and put together a good plan moving really good as you said in the first half, second half not as much. What would you identify there? >> Yeah, you know, I think uh I think the effort, the physicality of our unit, you know, up front and I think too it's the whole unit now. I mean, that's one thing we stress. Um, you know, it's not it's the receivers blocking, it's the tight end's blocking, it's it's the running back's finishing, it's the quarterback carrying out a keeper fake. Um, the one thing you can never question with our guys is their effort, their physicality, their play style, and I've been really proud of that through three weeks. Um, you know, I thought we were pretty sharp in terms of our fundamentals. That was a that was a big focus going into week three. Um, you know, I thought we did a good job in in the first half. There was a couple we can be a little bit cleaner in the second half and then, you know, some adjustments that we can make schematically, too. So, I think, you know, um kind of the second half adjustments, things like that, um some little tweaks here and there that that will help put us in in in more opportune situations. The other thing is, you know, we kind of fell behind. Um you know, that kind of a couple of those later drives were you trying to push the ball downfield in the pass game a little bit more, but um certainly want to expand off of what we did in the first half. Um was encouraged by that. just need to carry through in the second half with you know again some adjustments on our end as a staff and then um you know continue to lean into the fundamentals and play style for the unit. >> John, it seems like your high usage of 11 personnel seems to be tied a little bit to how the injuries you had had tied in starting with Eli and Dallas. Would you say that's fair um to why that number is there and how has it been kind of reframing how you are as an offense? Yeah, there's there's multiple factors to that and and you you hit on a couple of them already, right? You're you're managing injuries throughout the week. You're managing opponent and their tendencies, what they may be doing um with their personnels and how you want to attack that specifically. Um so, there's a couple factors there. Obviously, you know, you know, it's a shame, you know, Dallas getting dinged up in that Tennessee game. Um he's a big part of what we're doing. Um but we have a lot of good depth there. I know Zach came in on short notice and um you know, filled a filled a good role for us. Um, you know, we love what we have out of out of EJ and Johnny. Um, you know, really like that group, really like the receiver group. You know, it's it's it's a luxury for us that we feel we have the flexibility to do multiple things based on the opponent and based on whatever situation we have going on with our personnel. Um, some of it's injuries, some of it's the opponent. I guess to answer your question, it's a little bit of both week to week. >> Not with Devonte and Ottawa both doing some injuries. How does that grow things? Yeah, you know, I'm I'm not going to comment on on our upcoming plan for the Rams, but um like you said, you know, I think the nature of football, especially as you get deeper and deeper in the season, you know, it's only week four, but you're always going to be managing certain things. We had a we had a enough time I felt um that even if we played it short of the sticks we could go up and get a clock. Now it was um you know kind of a longer kind of push the pile type play towards the end zone and obviously that's you know we didn't want it to come that close. A heads up play by Jaylen to push it into the end zone but I'm not going to speak too much on the details of of our scheme there. Um, you know, obviously with 19 seconds left, I felt comfortable that if we were short of the sticks, we could get the ball clocked, but um, you know, it was, uh, it was, you know, heads up play by Jaylen and, um, you know, we almost scored on the screen there. You know, each week there's more and more um you know, data for opponents to go off of in terms of how I call games. Um you know, that's the kind of the luxury of the first couple weeks is I'm, you know, there there's no tendencies on me yet. Um but as you get going, you have to be more and more vigilant with how you monitor that. um you know, you know, Gummy in the Box, all of our coaches, they do a great job for me, kind of feeding me information on how I've been calling it. Um obviously each week it's a part of what we do is review our own self scout tendencies and um you know, I I think that's something that you're constantly looking at um to to make sure that you're, you know, you're not you're covering all your bases on your own selfcout end. >> You guys have been pretty consistent targeting on the the screen passes like the swing pass. >> Uh they've been going for negative yards, I guess. what are you seeing uh in terms of what's going on with those? >> Yeah, you know, I think ultimately, you know, we got to be better in the screen game. Obviously seemed like Jaylen would get most of the reps in practice, but as y'all are figuring out still um between Tanner and Andy and how are you how are you kind of uh how like rep situation and like finding the development there and going forward evaluation of that? >> Yeah, you know, I think that's the kind of the unseen part of practice. Um, but it's not just simply for Vic, you know, we're getting an opportunity to see these guys compete every day. They're get those are their reps. text: Hello everyone. Welcome to the weekly NFL preview show on Inside the Birds.  I'm Jeff Mosher.  It's week four in the NFL.  This is madness. The first half always flies by unnoticed. A bunch of injuries.  A bunch of injuries that affect all these games.  But I'll tell you this, there's something else that affects a lot of games that I want to talk about quickly before I get to the games.  Good.  During my more than 20 years of covering the Eagles and the NFL, I have had the honor and opportunity to attend training camps, owner meetings, meet the staff, and coaches.  I've met many people involved in the league who see the game differently.  And often, you know, I always talk about schemes, strategy or personnel.  But analytics and game management, things like that have become a bigger part of the discussions I try to have when I talk to people.  And the more I watch NFL football, the more I'm amazed by the coaches who I consider to be good coaches, good schemers, good people like "X" and "O." Even if they have bad results, sometimes it doesn't show who the coach really is.  But what often surprises me is how bad some coaches are at time management, time management, making decisions when games get tight and you have to make a decision that maybe is based on analytics, but it's just good football and smart football versus bad football.  I know you’re going to say, “Jeff, you covered the Andy Reid era.  What do you mean when you say you're surprised by poor time management? Yes, Andy Reid is a brilliant coach who was held back for a long time early in his career by poor time management.  And that's true.  Uh, I thought things were going to get better, overall decision-making, time management, time management, as we enter an era of so much analytics and so much, uh , resources available to you .  But we keep seeing games won and lost on this show last week.  I was talking about Aaron Glenn and his decision-making at the end of that game against the Packers, where he doesn't take timeouts, uh, to give his offense a chance to get the ball, it ends up going into overtime, and then makes an unpopular decision to take the ball, when most coaches always want to give the ball away and then they know what they need to do.  When you know what you need to do, it can better influence your decisions about the game than when you get the ball first and know that your opponent has a chance to score.  so you are probably less risky.  You don't want to take risks, it can make you naturally conservative, you just try to at least score a field goal, whereas you might know that if you have a good offense, especially if all I need to do is tie a field goal or score a touchdown, you have the advantage of being a little more aggressive.  Uh, but that was it, wasn't it? And then we also talked about week two when, uh, Eagles-Titans, and you saw Robert Saleh, who, you know, obviously left the Eagles too much time on the clock by kicking the ball into the end zone instead of a short punt and trying to kick off a return that would have taken time off the clock.  And then you saw a couple of games last weekend with similar bad decisions.  I don't need to go into all of them. Zach, what do you think is key for the offense to really improve its situational football, whether it's converting third chances or improving efficiency in the red zone ? Yes, I think it comes down to all 11 playing as one.  You know, execution above all else in all these situations.  There are certain calls where, you know, there are a couple of calls per game where I think, man, I put the guys in a bad position.  We ran an open zone in the second half of the game. They made a diagonal movement towards her.  Hey man, that wasn't a great call.  We had a one-yard loss, you know.  So there are things that, of course, we as those who call the plays want to do better.  And from the players' point of view, we've had, you know, many opportunities to take advantage of some of those.  And then, obviously, we've had some situations where we've been, you know, one step forward and two steps back.  So I think that more than anything , it's applicable to the situational, and some of those are first and second chances that put us in difficult situations.  We had a lot of long third chances last week that we need to clear by being efficient on first and second chances.  But, yes, I think it's simply about all 11 playing as one, being connected as a unit, and, you know, everyone trusting the person next to them to do their job and taking advantage of opportunities to mitigate, you know, like in the first game, the turnovers. And then the next two were a mix between, you know, holding on to a crucial third opportunity. Obviously, last week was the same.  So, each game has had its own rhythm in terms of those things from a situational point of view .  But we have to clean all that up;  These situations that arise are sometimes the product of the first and second chances that put us in a bind. What are the challenges of facing the Packers' seven frontcourt players? Yes, it's a talented group, a really talented group.  You know, I didn't know much about them, we haven't faced them in a long time.  And I know they have good young talent on the other side .  They are playing at a high level.  I know that last week's game seemed like an exception.  If you look at the first two games, they played exceptionally well.  So we expect them to be at their best, much like what happened with Cleveland;  When we played them in week two, we knew we would see a different team after their week one game.  So we expect them to be working at their best.  They have talent at all three levels.  They have a good safeties team. Linebackers know how to run and hit. We have some experience there with many players on that side of the ball .  So it will be a big challenge for our entire offense and we're looking forward to it. Zac, there's something universal about a rookie quarterback: he's going to receive a lot of pressure.  They're going to try it out with blitzes and things like that.  And how do you prepare for that? And what's it like being a starter in the NFL? Well, I was never a starter.  But if I had been , I don't know, JD is much calmer than I am.  So it's hard to say what that would have been like.  But, yes , you can anticipate that, well, you have a young guy there.  They might present confusing diagrams that were not in the videos, to try to disorient you, distract your vision from the progression and reading, and from making protective adjustments.  So, we'll do a great job if we have to adjust things during the game.  We based our decision on what we have seen and, perhaps, on some things from the past with this coordinator.  That's why we'll be prepared for anything.  But, as you said, with a rookie quarterback, you have to anticipate untested schemes.  All you have to do is play American football, receive the ball, trust your decisions, your reads, and keep going.  Furthermore , the good thing about him is that he can also run away .  And you've seen that throughout the preseason.  That 's the best thing for a young boy: to be able to run and get out of tricky situations, which he does very well.    We haven't seen much of Qadree Ollison on offense.  Is he a player who could be more involved given his skill set? 100%.  We need to get Tuck up and running.  He's special with the ball in his hands, as you've already seen during your time here.  That depends on us as coaches.  We need to find time to integrate it. Again, considering the pace of some plays where we end up in long second and third down situations. Knowing that he is more of a runner for first and second chances.  So we have to include it.  That is our responsibility as coaches.  But we expect that Tuck, when he receives those opportunities, will undoubtedly take advantage of them. Has the coach been involved in anything?  We saw it in practice, but I know it's very competitive.  It must be difficult for him not to be there, but has he been involved in helping? Ah, yes.  Coach Baker is very present and active.  He's doing a great job helping JD.  You know, we just signed Brett Rypien, who is another veteran presence in that room.  It's a great group of guys, you know, but yeah, Bake has been there .  He's as focused on the game plan as if he were playing, and that's Bake for you, as you know.  It's very competitive.  He just wants us to win the game however we have to .  So, uh, he's done a great job with JD taking him aside after a series of plays in practice, and he's been very focused. He knows everything we're trying to achieve from a game plan perspective.  It has been a great help to JD, and I know it will help him on game day too. Zac said Hamler had that explosive play last week against the Vikings, but how do you want to involve him more, have him make more contact within this offense? Yes, I think that, similar to the rest of the skilled players, coverage can dictate where some things go at certain times.  He definitely had some opportunities to possibly make a couple more contacts.  And he didn't find the ball last week for one reason or another, but yes, we need to keep Ted active.  He's done a great job, man.  I can't say enough good things about him.  It was great to see his first touchdown in that.  It was a great play.  Obviously, we were losing 10-0.  We needed a spark.  It was great protection, a great job by Bake to see it, and he ran a great route to finish it.  So, I really need to find ways for all these guys.  We have a unique skill set to which we can distribute the ball.  And so, it could be a game where someone gets fired up .  They're getting a few more contacts, but Ted is doing a great job.  It is achieving separation.  It's open. We definitely have to find him when he is.  Brilliant.  I appreciate it, Zac.

title: The 49ers and a TRADE pursuit of T.J. Watt…
text: So, it's officially October, which means that the significant impact trade market for the 49ers isn't all that far from opening up. Just watched the Steelers lose last night. No, they're not in sell mode yet. But if they did ever approach sell mode with a few more losses over October, they do have TJ Watt, who's about to turn 32, superstar. They do have Alex Heismith, who's still in his 20s. two more years left on his contract, maybe a more manageable trade target for the 49ers. But I'm going to ask you guys in a little bit what you'd be willing to trade for TJ Watt. Start thinking about it because I'll remind you of that question in just a little bit. Couple other potential names to watch on a team that isn't good that's 0 and three right now. Khalil Mack and Dalvin Tomlinson. Mack is an edge rusher, obviously, one of the great edge rushers ever. And Tom Linson is a defensive tackle who's playing much much better this season than he did last season. Both of those guys now with the Chargers who are 0 and three. And both of them on one-year deals. You know, it might be that the 49ers go for a defensive tackle over a defensive end. With the fiveman fronts they're running, they do need a lot of bodies at defensive tackle. They've lost a lot of bodies there. But the whole Nick Bosa thing, we have to look at it in terms of both a short-term and long-term proposition. How do the 49ers fortify themselves at edge? Not just this season because it's so important, but in seasons past this one. And along those lines, what would you give up for Alex Heismith? A really, really good edge rusher, a younger edge rusher, a lighter edge rusher for the Pittsburgh Steelers. And never say never. We saw Miles Garrett move teams away from the AFC North to the NFC West. What would you give up for TJ Watt? I want to see the answers in the comments section. He's got 30 plus million guaranteed this year and still 30 plus million guaranteed next season just for what it's worth and under contract through the season after that through 2028. Anyway, we talked about all the dynamics with the 49ers and their injury situation on 95.7 the game. Have a listen. >> It's David Lombardi everybody here on Willlet and Dibs. Hi David. What's going on? >> Not much. How you guys doing? I'm going to enjoy I'm going to enjoy this weather in San Francisco, but I don't think it's going to be too enjoyable in Santa Clara over the next few days. You guys see this? 94 on Sunday down there, >> which means it's going to be over triple digits probably on the field, >> man. On the sunny side of the street. >> Yeah. You know, the 49ers ain't caught a break that just didn't come for Miami or Arizona because those are two teams. We've seen Arizona beat the 49ers wear them down in one of those hot weather games because they practice outside. So, um I think that they would be better equipped to take advantage of that. So, it's good for the 49ers. They're playing Denver, not one of those two hot weather teams. >> Yeah. So, and and I feel obviously for the fans that are on the uh the other side of the stadium. Um too bad it's not a night game, but but here we go. Uh there are always challenges and the wide receiver core is is obviously one of the main ones for the Niners this weekend. David, what do you think? What how does this affect the team? What should we expect with that group? >> I wouldn't be so quick to rule Mike Evans out. I'll tell you what. I step in the locker room on Wednesday and Mike Evans has his jersey on and so does Trent Williams and that means that they both participated in the walkthrough. They're sitting there playing cards. Guys who are so seriously hurt that there's very little chance they're going to play are not sitting in the locker room playing cards. They're rehabbing around the clock. Like so I I think with Mike Evans and to a degree with Trent Williams, we're going to have to be ready for constant management throughout this season. And I think that Mike Evans, as we heard John Lynch say when he was doing his interview this morning, uh he he's a guy that's going to really fight hard to play. Now, there is a scenario in which the 49ers tell Mike and Mike reluctantly agrees that hey, Seattle's coming up next week. What do you need to do to be over 90% for Seattle? If that involves you sitting this week, then then fine. or they could carry six receivers active on Sunday and maybe Mike Evans has a lessened role to make sure or to maximize the chances that he's a little bit more ready for the game against Seattle. So, it's just one of the the byproducts of having a team that's as old as the 49ers are offensively um is that there's going to be a whole lot more this guy doesn't have to practice to actually play going on. and we've already seen a lot of that from the 49ers and with with Mike Evans this season. title: Commanders Offensive Line Answered the Call Against Seattle | Film Session
text: That's right.  Welcome again to another Chop Film film session.  I'm your host of the Chop Film podcast, Marley Moe, Jamal Ford.  Let's analyze the play of the Washington Commanders offensive line.  You wouldn't have won that game against the Seattle Seahawks without the effort and competitiveness of that offensive line.  And I understand that if you have complaints about the players or a specific player in this unit, it is completely justified.  I understand that.  I'm not offended by you.  And these are the things Washington has to deal with in the offseason.  But we're where we are now, and I think all five guys: Nick Allegretti, Patrick Lucas, or Lucas Patrick , whatever his name is, right?  Newcomer.  Brandon Coleman, Chris Paul, Josh Connelly.  All five won.  And we should mention the tight ends and wide receivers at some points as well.  And I think all of that is important when you look at the success in the passing game and the takeaway game , the way that offensive line has played .  So, if no one is going to give them any credit beyond a quick salute, let's take a look at a few game moments that showcase their efforts, how well they played, and perhaps whether they have any future prospects.  So, without further ado, hit the like button, subscribe button.  The Chop it Up filming session is starting right now.  So, let's deal with one of the first gameplay moments.  As the game went on, the takeaway game kind of ...it kind of dissolved, but they never stopped fighting.    The physical presence was palpable.  And early in the game, Washington really had good opportunities for big breakthroughs ahead.  Right here, you get a quick seven-yard gain. But what's important here is when you look at how well they performed in this episode: your tight ends, one goes to the second level, the other works on the front end.  And then you find yourself on the first level, sorry, on the cutting edge.  And then there's Terry McLaurin running to try to take a Seattle defender out of the game , right?  So you get blocking from John Bostick, a good double guard between Josh Garnett and Nick Allegretti, but it's really a combo block because Allegretti helps as a support player before blocking the zone or going up to the second level, right?  And then you see Terry providing that overlap too.  We're talking about setting the tone from the beginning.  It's the first quarter, just a few plays have passed, maybe the fourth play. Let's see.  Yes, the fourth draw of the game.  You get a very good, let's say , balanced run that ultimately helps Washington in this episode. Throughout the game, you've seen Marcus deal with some...not even deal with.  You saw Marcus throw the ball from really good, comfortable pockets, right?  Here you see several things at work, honestly, several factors at once. You get a 3x2 offset defense and essentially a personal guard on the left flank, right?  So Leonard Williams—our guy right here, right above Nick Allegretti, Josh Garnett, and Luke Gatsey.  Patrick shifts to the right. Since you're doing a three- player offset, you're getting a real double-guard on Leonard Williams, who's the main threat, right?  You need to make sure you take it into account .  So you get this lock.  Josh Garnett has one-on- one, but Nick Allegretti comes in and helps, right?  So you get essentially a three-on-two action, and Nick Allegretti is a workhorse.  He's the one looking for work, and that's exactly what he's doing, right?  And then on the left side you have two one-on- one confrontations, personal blocking.  Chris Paul is going too far back, but he's able to recover with his shot, right?  And just push it out and make it run in an arc.  Eventually he returns to the starting position with his feet, right?  And Rashad Wright's push helps him, but then you see him make the block anyway.  We are doing well here.  And then Brandon Coleman on your left side, also a personal blocker.  And I think what's important when you look at Brandon Coleman is how he starts.  It's more of a vertical retreat, a vertical stand.  His feet are on the right footing, his footwork is good, but he also gets forward very quickly, which is also good. And it starts...it starts with that, but then the hands start moving.  It's a downward rebound...He's a guy who likes to grab and trap .  If you're going to get your hands on Brian O'Callaghan, chances are you'd better have good timing or play smart games and have a backup plan.  He will simply knock your hands down.  He tries to stay as "clean" as possible in the game.  And ultimately, what this does here, and you'll see a few more examples, is it just stops the flow.  Stops the pressure.  A clean pocket for throwing.  And you can't ask for anything better if you're Marcus Mariota.  This is a draw you would like to replay.
